If you're near Palo Alto or Singapore that means day-of execution; if you're remote it means planning, partner outreach, and turning what happens into content - Turn every event into content: capture footage and conversations on site, then ship it while the moment is still warm - Run distribution experiments, then double down on what compounds and cut what doesn't - Track what actually moves: reach, engagement quality, click-through, signups, not vanity counts - Work with engineering and design to turn new features into content worth sharing - Develop taste for what earns attention honestly, without resorting to hype YOU MIGHT BE A FIT IF - You're pursuing a Bachelor's or Master's degree in any field, or equivalent experience - You've built and run your own channel, newsletter, community, or feed, and can show it - You have real distribution outcomes, even small ones, and you can explain what worked and what flopped - You're comfortable on camera or behind an edit, and you ship quickly - You have strong written voice and instinct for what makes people stop scrolling - You're genuinely curious about AI and can explain technical ideas to a general audience - You're comfortable in a room full of strangers, and you'd rather run the event than attend it. If you're remote, you're still willing to own events end to end from a distance Bonus: video editing, motion graphics, experience organizing events or hackathons, or an existing audience in tech
